answers.reasoning: For the supplied perpendicular static point load, 5×9.8×1=49 N·m. The fourth source row and target match; this is not a printed derivation.
One affine scalar output b0+b1x1+b2x2 is a plane in the three-dimensional joint input-output space; p804 explicitly states two features: a plane.
The bilinear product 9.8mr includes an interaction. An affine raw-feature plane has constant partial slopes and no mr term; its intercept cannot supply a variable interaction.

The cause is explicitly missing informative inputs, with converged optimization. Measure the missing relevant variables; capacity or repeated optimization on indistinguishable incomplete inputs cannot restore missing information.
Iteration count is only a possible risk in iterative fitting. Held-out error, not training improvement or a transferred epoch count alone, determines whether continued fitting damages generalization.
Distance in temperature/Wi-Fi feature space does not impose connectivity in physical space. Identical sensor readings can arise in disconnected rooms, so the plot does not guarantee geographic zones.
Normal location and scale specify mean and standard deviation, not hard bounds. The actual p815 upper cluster contains points above 100 percent, consistent with the unclipped Gaussian example.
A single bijective relabeling preserves all pairwise same-cluster relationships. Arbitrary independent point-label changes do not; numeric zone IDs have no inherent quality ordering.

The table motivates anomaly detection using abnormal torque patterns. Unusualness alone cannot distinguish a mechanical failure, sensor fault or changed operation; the inference is a qualified application of the table premise.

Grouping similar colors permits a smaller palette and indices with possible reconstruction loss. Retaining all original values plus labels is not itself compression; overhead qualification is appropriate.
The set contains allowed moves; left is one selected element. The slide incorrectly calls the whole set Action(a), so the correction distinguishes the set from the chosen move.

The repeated p818 action/reward loop permits feedback after a step, while p817 describes delayed sequence feedback. Both fit RL; delayed outcomes can depend on earlier choices and require credit assignment.

A responsive simulator can implement action-conditioned transitions, observations and rewards. A fixed route log alone does not provide counterfactual interaction; physical hardware is not part of the functional requirement.
